meta_title: VpnHood! SERVER: Open-Source VPN Server for Linux & Windows
meta_description: Free, open-source VPN server for Linux, Windows and Docker. One pasted command, port 443 by default, TCP, UDP and QUIC, and Cloak Mode against blocking.
page_title: VpnHood! SERVER: free, open-source VPN server software
page_desc: The engine of your VPN. It runs on your own machine, carries your users' traffic, and answers to nobody's infrastructure but yours.
f_anywhere_desc: Linux (x64 or ARM64), Windows, or Docker: any VPS or dedicated machine from any provider, installed with a single pasted command. It listens on port 443 out of the box, with no network configuration.
f_stealth_title: Hard to spot, harder to block
f_stealth_desc: With Cloak Mode, the tunnel is shaped to look like ordinary web traffic, and an unauthenticated probe gets a plain web-server response instead of anything worth testing. No network is guaranteed to let it through, but there is little to match against.
f_engine_desc: VpnHood! ENGINE keeps the connection encrypted and stable across hostile networks, over TCP, UDP and QUIC, with IPv4 and IPv6 support.
f_open_desc: Every line is public on GitHub under the LGPL, and the project has been audited by Include Security for the Open Technology Fund's Red Team Lab. Nothing to take on faith.
run_manager_desc: The free panel installs the server for you, watches it live, and issues your access keys. Add more servers and it balances users across them. The easiest path for most people.
run_solo_desc: No panel required: a built-in file-based access manager lets a single server issue its own keys, configured from a simple settings file. On Linux, vhserver gen prints a new one.
setup_guide: Setup guide: install on Windows, Linux, or Docker
cta: Free, open-source, and ready for your server.
hero_alt: A server rack on a plinth, a shielded tunnel leaving it, and three small device screens connecting back to it
prod_desc: The details that decide whether a VPN server is something you set up once or something you babysit.
prod_1: Hot restart: restart or update the server and open sessions carry on.
prod_2: No administrator rights required. On Linux it can even run without root.
prod_3: Network-scan protection stops users scanning networks through your server, which keeps your IP out of abuse reports.
prod_4: Works behind a reverse proxy such as Cloudflare, and still sees each client's real IP.
prod_5: Speed and traffic limits: with MANAGER, each plan sets how much and how fast its keys may use.
run_note: Either way, your users connect with VpnHood! CLIENT, free on Android, iOS, Windows and Linux. Your own white-labelled app can connect to the same servers.
